title: Men's Golf Major Championships
blurb: Career men's major titles from the first Open Championship at Prestwick in 1860. Vardon's six Claret Jugs stand for a decade until Walter Hagen passes him in 1926; Nicklaus then rewrites the record to 18, and Tiger Woods's charge stalls three short at 15.

source.name: Official records of the Masters, PGA of America, USGA and The R&A
source.note: Modern four-major convention: Masters, U.S. Open, The Open and PGA Championship only, so Bobby Jones has 7. Amateur titles excluded.

milestones.title: Young Tom's four in a row
milestones.text: Tom Morris Jr. wins his fourth straight Open (none was held in 1871), aged 21. He dies three years later at 24.

milestones.title: Vardon's sixth Open
milestones.text: Harry Vardon wins a record sixth Open Championship for his seventh major, the benchmark for the next decade.

milestones.title: Hagen passes Vardon
milestones.text: Walter Hagen's third straight PGA Championship gives him eight majors, taking the record from Harry Vardon.

milestones.title: Jones's Grand Slam
milestones.text: Bobby Jones wins the U.S. Open and Open plus both amateur titles, then retires at 28 with 7 pro-era majors.

milestones.title: Nicklaus passes Hagen
milestones.text: The 1973 PGA is Nicklaus's 12th major, passing Hagen's 11. Counting amateurs (14), it also beat Jones's 13.

milestones.title: Nicklaus's 18th at 46
milestones.text: Jack Nicklaus shoots 30 on the back nine to win the Masters at 46, his 18th and final major.

milestones.title: Woods reaches 14
milestones.text: Tiger Woods wins the U.S. Open on a broken leg for major No. 14, four short of Nicklaus at age 32.

milestones.title: Tiger's 15th, then stalls
milestones.text: An 11-year drought ends with the 2019 Masters, Woods's 15th major. It proves to be his last; Nicklaus's 18 stands.
